description: We are a student team from Alanya, Türkiye, combining our interests in space science, research, and storytelling. For Abandoned but not Forgotten, we will investigate equipment left on the Moon and Mars, then tell younger readers what it did and what it helped us discover.
summary:
The Robot That Bounced on the Moon is a five-scene interactive story about Surveyor 3, a lander that remained on the Moon after its mission ended. Young readers click through its imagined narration to discover its bouncing landing, the marks its scoop made in lunar soil, and the Apollo 12 astronauts’ visit more than two years later. A separate facts and sources panel distinguishes the storytelling from documented events.

The project addresses “Abandoned but Not Forgotten” by showing that equipment left behind can still have a story and scientific value. Parts of Surveyor 3 returned to Earth for study, extending what scientists could learn from its mission. We hope the story makes that history accessible to children and sparks curiosity about what future explorers will leave behind.
details:
Our project, The Robot That Bounced on the Moon, is a five-scene interactive story for young readers. Surveyor 3 tells the story in an imagined voice, from its bumpy landing and lunar soil tests to the Apollo 12 astronauts’ visit more than two years later. Readers click the dialogue box or use the arrow keys to reveal the story a little at a time. A “Facts & sources” button links to NASA and JPL records and explains where the storytelling takes creative liberty.

We wanted children to see how a machine left on the Moon could still teach us that the universe is full of discoveries. The story connects Surveyor 3’s observations of the ground with the later examination of parts brought back to Earth. Its final question invites readers to think about what future explorers might leave behind.

Our team researched the mission, wrote and revised the narration, and checked the scientific claims. We built the website with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript and published it on Vercel. ChatGPT helped us fact-check, build the website, and generate the five illustrations. Each illustration is visibly marked “SI-GENERATED.” We chose a bright comic style and a familiar game-like dialogue box to make the history inviting and nostalgic, while keeping the imagined voice separate from documented mission events.
